packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-15 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author before or during this reading. I have not tried to identify it.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

The packet shows four faces (two pieces, each photographed on both sides, as far as I can tell from shape; this pairing is my inference).

- image-001 (overview), tiles image-002, image-003: a tall narrow paper strip, upright. Writing survives only along the right edge: the first 2-6 letters of about 21 lines, the rest cut away. Most of the strip is blank (a wide left margin). One Roman numeral "III." begins a line; a blank interval and an indented start near the bottom suggest a new paragraph.
- image-004 (overview), tiles image-005, image-006: a tall narrow strip (probably the other side of the same strip - inference), upright. Writing survives only along the left edge: the last few letters of about 20 lines, then two short centred lines at the foot. Double-stroke hyphens („) mark word-breaks at line ends.
- image-007 (overview), tiles image-008, image-009: a wider piece with a vertical fold/join. Left of the fold: the right-hand part of a single text block, about 21 lines, line-beginnings lost at the left edge; one short heading line set off by space. Right of the fold: a short centred block headed by a Latin scriptural reference, then five lines of Greek, then a large pen flourish; the rest blank. Tentative interpretation: the Greek block closes the text (end-piece).
- image-010 (overview), tiles image-011, image-012: the other side (inference). Left of the fold blank. Right of the fold: the left-hand part of a text block, about 22 lines, line-ends lost at the right edge. A numbered heading "VII. De Prophanatione" in slightly larger letters; numbered items "I." and "II."; at the foot a mark that looks like a quire signature.

Script: a small upright italic/humanistic cursive in brown ink, with printed-style conventions (ae-ligature, ampersand, „ hyphens, Roman section numbers, a signature mark). No rubrics, no coloured initials, no underlining, no interlinear or marginal glosses seen. No running titles visible (top edges are torn).

2. AREAS SELECTED

All visible writing on all four faces is transcribed; the text is short. Nothing legible was left unread except the first (cut) line on image-012 and image-008.

4. OBSERVATIONS vs. INTERPRETATION

Observed: a numbered section VII headed "De Prophanatione" with numbered examples I (Ierobaam) and II (Nebuzar Adan), a third name "Antiocho" announced; on the other face a passage naming "[A]ntiochus", citing "1. Macchab: 1." and "Bernhardus", followed by a heading ending "-ilogus" and a closing paragraph, then a Greek scriptural text headed "1. Petri. 3." with "Amen" and a flourish.
Tentative: Face D precedes Face C (the three names announced on D; the third treated at the top of C), with at least one face of text between them not present here. The narrow strips (Faces A, B) are in the same hand and may be the conjugate stub of the same bifolium; the fragments "III.", "Eccle-", "-esiam", "domum / Dei" would fit the same subject, but nothing joins them line-to-line.
I have not expanded lost line-ends or line-beginnings.

5. LIMITATIONS

- Every text block is cut vertically: Faces A and B keep only a few letters per line; Faces C and D lose roughly a third to a half of each line.
- Top edges torn: first line of image-008 and image-012 only partly visible.
- The Greek is in a ligatured hand; accents/breathings in my transcription are normalised from what the ligatures appear to represent, not letter-by-letter observation.
- The heading reference above the Greek reads to me as "1. Petri. 3."; the numerals are small and I could be misreading the first.
- A wider view is not needed; what would help is the missing halves of the leaves.

Reader activity: opened READER.md; PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg through image-012.jpg (all twelve); attempted image-013.jpg (does not exist). Also opened the files of packet-12 listed in that response. Nothing else.
